pr_title: e2e: Remove kubeadm-ism in DNS HostNetwork test
pr_body:
The "[sig-network] DNS HostNetwork should resolve DNS of partial qualified names for services on hostNetwork pods with dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet" test assumes that a service named "kube-dns" exists in the "kube-system" namespace.  This assumption is valid if the cluster was configured using kubeadm, but the assumption may be invalid otherwise.

As the test uses `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` (as opposed to `dnsPolicy: None`), it does not need to specify `dnsConfig.nameservers`.  Omitting `dnsConfig.nameservers` obviates the need to look up the service.

Follow-up to #112824.

* `test/e2e/network/dns.go`: Don't look up or use the "kube-dns" cluster IP address as it might not exist on clusters that were not configured using kubeadm.

issue_context.title: E2E test for for ExpandedDNSConfig has a kubeadm-ism
issue_context.body:
### Which jobs are flaking?

#112824 added an E2E test that assumes that a service named "kube-dns" exists in the "kube-system" namespace.  This is a kubeadm-ism, and the test fails if the cluster DNS is not configured the way kubeadm configures it.  

Although this E2E test isn't a conformance test, making it functional on non-kubeadm clusters would increase its utility for distributors that may wish to run this E2E test as a conformance test.  

### Which tests are flaking?

[sig-network] DNS HostNetwork should resolve DNS of partial qualified names for services on hostNetwork pods with dnsPolicy: ClusterFirstWithHostNet

### Since when has it been flaking?

Since we ran it on an OpenShift cluster.  https://github.com/openshift/kubernetes/pull/1432

### Testgrid link

_No response_

### Reason for failure (if possible)

The test makes assumptions about how the cluster DNS is configured.  

### Anything else we need to know?

The test uses `dnsPolicy: ClusterFirst` (not `dnsPolicy: None`), so it does not need to specify `dnsConfig.nameservers`, as far as I can tell.  Omitting `dnsConfig.nameservers` obviates the need to look up the service.  I believe that the service lookup was left in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/112824 as an oversight during the development of the test when it was changed from specifying "None" to specifying "ClusterFirst": https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/compare/5fcdde0a0a82b052bb67cd764150725f2ca73dd9..1098ff63f34673ef9eec06572cbfaf49cea93222

Cc: @gjkim42

### Relevant SIG(s)

/sig network
